candidate: Predictive AV1 changes in this commit; development version 0.3.2. Browser reporting refinements followed the native trials and do not change native processing.

environment.native_build: Rust 1.95.0, Cargo release, locked dependencies, both binaries built with the same compiler/profile
environment.transport_runner: Bun 1.4.2, same runner for both binaries; ordinary CI/development uses Bun 1.3.13

method: Three interleaved before/after trials for each input; 600 frames, two requests outstanding, first 30 excluded. Moving input is 120 tightly packed 1080p NV12 frames cycled from the first two seconds of the prior FFmpeg testsrc2 fixture. SHA-256 is retained per trial. No concurrent build/browser fixture/other benchmark; normal desktop applications remained open. Data retain every completion and selected stage fields; warm summaries exclude startup. GPU usage, CPU usage and RSS were not sampled in this comparison.

audio.source: 4 seconds, 880 Hz sine, amplitude 0.2, 48000 Hz; 200–206 ms decode age; interrupted fades, repeated bypass, reattach
audio.notes: Actual OfflineAudioContext nodes/automation with a scheduled control clock. Undelayed reference rendered simultaneously. Excludes physical audio devices, underruns and audible A/V synchronization. --legacy-ref supports the single-delay graph in v0.3.2 and earlier.

decode_validation.static: 60/60 real 4K AV1 pictures decoded by ffprobe
decode_validation.moving: 180/180 real 4K AV1 pictures decoded by ffprobe, including periodic IDR
decode_validation.restart: Six 720p pictures with a forced same-size restart at picture four; 6/6 decoded

limits: Native transport throughput is not browser presentation FPS.
Static content strongly favors inter prediction; moving fixture throughput was essentially unchanged while packets fell about 15%.

Visible Brave 155 hardware AV1 decode and lifecycle passed with ambient Bun/CDP, but presentation was about 12 FPS. A pinned Bun/native-CDP run connected and presented initially but failed sustained presentation. Cause is unresolved; no 4K browser speedup is claimed for this patch.
Chromium 148 360p-to-720p GPU lifecycle and sustained-presentation checks passed on final browser code, with hidden state emulated.
The offline audio test measures actual browser automation/waveforms under a scheduled control clock, not physical listening, device underruns or audible A/V offset.
No new 8K throughput, natural-video quality, long-run CPU/RSS, or upstream Python parity claims.
